task.description: Re-check (step-01c) of CODE-DESIGNER's rework1 of lib/letflow/design/req203-artifact-activation.md against the four findings from step-01b (OQ-A, OQ-E, OQ-F, §2.4 inconsistency).
acceptance_criteria: OQ-A: §2.2/§0 state new_version_number as :bigint directly, citation verified against the migration file
OQ-E: {:error, :duplicate_artifact_in_group} in §4.1's error union, explicit pre-Multi step 1b
OQ-F: one Letflow.Audit.append_multi/4 call per artifact stated as committed in §4.2/§7
§2.4: changeset mechanism corrected to validate_required(:rationale) alone, whitespace-only behavior verified against actual Ecto 3.14.1 cast/4 semantics
§9 lists only OQ-B/OQ-C, both re-confirmed as legitimate deferrals
No new inconsistency introduced by the edit

result.summary:
Three of the four prior findings are genuinely fixed. (1) OQ-A: verified priv/repo/migrations/20260830030001_create_repository_artifacts.exs:88 declares 'add :version_number, :bigint, null: false' -- matches §0/§2.2's now-direct ':bigint' statement, no deferral remains, OQ-A correctly removed from §9. (2) OQ-E: §4.1's signature now includes '{:error, :duplicate_artifact_in_group}' in the return-type union, and §4.2 step 1b states an explicit pre-Multi check (build (artifact_kind, artifact_name) tuple list, compare length against Enum.uniq/1's length, return the error atom immediately on mismatch, before any Multi step is built) -- this is a committed, fully specified design decision, not a punt. (3) OQ-F: §4.2 step 3e and §7's narrative commit unambiguously to one Letflow.Audit.append_multi/4 call per artifact activated (inside that artifact's own Multi.run/3 step), with the granularity reasoning (matching artifact_activation_history's own one-row-per-artifact convention) stated as a design decision, not left to ELIXIR-DEV. All three BLOCKERs are resolved.

However, the fourth finding's fix (§2.4) introduces a NEW, independently-verified factual defect that is at least as serious as the one it replaced, so this re-check FAILS.

§2.4 now claims: 'validate_required(:rationale), and nothing more... What this layer explicitly does NOT reject: a whitespace-only string (e.g. " ", a single space). " " is neither nil nor "", so cast/4 never nils it out and validate_required/2 never sees it as missing -- a caller submitting a rationale of pure whitespace passes the changeset layer unmodified.' This claim is FALSE for this codebase's actual pinned Ecto version, and I verified this two ways, not by trusting the restated claim: (a) source reading of deps/ecto/lib/ecto/changeset.ex's cast/4 pipeline -- cast_field/9 (changeset.ex:894) computes `filter_values(type, value, filter_values, defaults, key)` (changeset.ex:897), which calls the boolean lambda `filter_values.(type, value)` (changeset.ex:774: `fn type, value -> trim_values.(type, value) in empty_values end`); the default `trim_values` is `Ecto.Type.trim/2` (changeset.ex:760), and deps/ecto/lib/ecto/type.ex:1007 defines `def trim(type, value) when is_binary(value) and type != :binary, do: String.trim_leading(value)`. For an all-whitespace string like "   ", `String.trim_leading("   ")` returns `""`, which IS a member of `empty_values` (default `[""]`) -- so the boolean lambda returns `true`, `filter_values/5` returns `:empty`, and cast_field/9 replaces the value with `Map.get(defaults, key)` (nil, for an un-defaulted field) BEFORE `Ecto.Type.cast/2` even runs. The whitespace string is converted to `nil` by `cast/4` itself, exactly the same path `cast/4` already takes for a literal `""` -- `validate_required/2` then correctly reports it as missing. (b) Empirical verification: I ran this codebase's actual Ecto 3.14.1 dependency (via `elixir` under `~/.asdf/shims`, `MIX_ENV=test mix run --no-start`) against a throwaway schema module with a `:string` field and `cast(params, [:rationale]) |> validate_required(:rationale)`, identical to the design's stated mechanism: `changeset(%{}, %{"rationale" => "   "})` produced `valid?: false`, `errors: [rationale: {"can't be blank", [validation: :required]}]`, `changes: %{}` -- i.e. `validate_required(:rationale)` DOES reject a whitespace-only rationale in this codebase's actual runtime, contradicting the design's explicit claim that it 'passes the changeset layer unmodified.' (Real text validated as `valid?: true` in the same run, confirming the test harness itself is sound and not misconfigured.) Test files (lib/test_schema_tmp.ex, test_ws_check.exs) were created only as scratch verification and have been deleted; no change to tracked files.

This is not a cosmetic wording nit: the design's entire closing decision in §2.4 ('Whitespace-only rationale: decided out of scope, stated explicitly... this design deliberately does not add a validate_change/3-with-String.trim/1 check... A caller who submits "   " as a rationale gets it accepted and stored verbatim by both layers described above; this is an accepted, explicitly-stated gap, not an oversight') is reasoning from a false premise. The premise ('the changeset layer does not reject whitespace-only input') is wrong; the actual mechanism already specified (validate_required(:rationale) via the standard cast/4 pipeline) DOES reject a purely-whitespace rationale as a side effect of Ecto's default trim_leading-based empty-value detection. The DB-level CHECK (rationale <> '') genuinely still would not catch a value that somehow bypassed the changeset (e.g. a raw Repo.insert_all/3 with a literal whitespace string), so that half of §2.4's gap analysis is directionally fine, but the changeset-layer claim is factually wrong as written and must be corrected, not merely restated. This exact category of defect (a stated mechanism not matching its claimed effect) is the same class of error step-01b already failed on for the prior draft's validate_length claim -- it has recurred in the opposite direction after the rework, which is exactly why this gate re-verifies claims against source/runtime rather than trusting a restated correction.

The same false premise is repeated in §10's AC6 traceability row ('whitespace-only is a stated, deliberate non-goal per AC6's literal wording') and must be corrected in the same pass.

OQ-B and OQ-C (§9) were re-checked against the same standard applied to OQ-A/E/F: both remain legitimate deferrals. OQ-B (Ecto.Enum value-list sharing mechanism across four schema modules) is a pure Elixir-organization choice with no behavioral consequence the design needs to pin down now -- unlike OQ-A/E/F, there is no 'already-known answer' being withheld; any sharing mechanism ELIXIR-DEV picks (module attribute, shared function) produces identical runtime behavior, so this is correctly left to Step 2a. OQ-C (nullable activator_user_id for a hypothetical system/scheduler-driven activation) is grounded in the requirement's own text describing no such call path today, mirrors req195's own precedent for the analogous question, and does not have a discoverable 'right answer' sitting in a file the design already named the way OQ-A did -- it is a genuine future-scope question, not a resolvable fact or an already-decided-but-unstated design choice. Neither needs further action.

Traceability spot-check on AC6's row: structurally still points to the right section (§2.4), but inherits the false whitespace-rejection claim described above and must be corrected alongside it. No other new inconsistency found on a fresh read-through of the full document; §1, §3, §4.3, §5, §6, §8 are unchanged from the version already found correct in step-01b, and §7's OQ-F commitment is internally consistent with §4.2 step 3e.

issues.description: §2.4's claim that validate_required(:rationale) does NOT reject a whitespace-only rationale (e.g. " ") is factually wrong for this codebase's pinned Ecto 3.14.1. cast/4's default trim_values (Ecto.Type.trim/2, deps/ecto/lib/ecto/type.ex:1007) applies String.trim_leading/1 to a binary value before checking membership in empty_values; for an all-whitespace string this yields "", which is a member of the default empty_values ([""]), so cast/4 converts the whitespace-only value to nil before validate_required/2 ever runs -- validate_required/2 therefore DOES reject it. Verified both from deps/ecto/lib/ecto/changeset.ex source (cast_field/9 at line 894, filter_values/3 at line 937, using trim_values from line 760) and empirically (this codebase's actual Ecto dependency, via `MIX_ENV=test mix run --no-start` against a throwaway schema/changeset identical in shape to the design's stated mechanism: whitespace-only input produced valid?: false, errors: [rationale: {"can't be blank", ...}]). §2.4's closing 'decided out of scope' paragraph and its premise must be corrected to state the actual (opposite) behavior; §10's AC6 traceability row repeats the same false premise and needs the same correction.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- correct §2.4 (and §10's AC6 row) to state that validate_required(:rationale), via this codebase's actual cast/4 pipeline, already rejects whitespace-only rationale as a side effect of Ecto's default trim-leading empty-value detection (cite deps/ecto/lib/ecto/type.ex:1007 and the cast_field/9 path), and re-derive whatever narrower gap (if any) genuinely remains open (e.g. a value with internal-but-not-leading whitespace such as " x " is NOT caught by trim_leading and is NOT converted to nil, so a rationale like " a " still passes both layers -- if this is the actual residual gap, it must be described accurately, not conflated with the pure-whitespace case the design currently and incorrectly claims passes through).
